events.label: Holmes states that life is stranger than anything invented by the mind

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: "life is infinitely stranger than anything which the mind of man could invent."

events.label: Holmes states that one can look over the city and remove roofs to see strange coincidences and event chains

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: "If we could fly out of that window hand in hand, hover over this great city, gently remove the roofs, and peep in at the queer things which are going on, the strange coincidences, the plannings, the cross-purposes, the wonderful chains of events, working through generations, and leading to the most outré results, it would make all fiction with its conventionalities and foreseen conclusions most stale and unprofitable."

communicates.speaker: doctor_watson
communicates.content: "We have in our police reports realism pushed to its extreme limits, and yet the result is, it must be confessed, neither fascinating nor artistic."

events.label: Holmes remarks that selection and discretion are needed for a realistic effect

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: "A certain selection and discretion must be used in producing a realistic effect,"

events.label: Holmes contrasts police report stress on magistrate platitudes vs vital details

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: "This is wanting in the police report, where more stress is laid, perhaps, upon the platitudes of the magistrate than upon the details, which to an observer contain the vital essence of the whole matter."

events.label: Holmes says there is nothing so unnatural as the commonplace
